summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 3 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.29/1341)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: E kətwo. I naqqayo ḥaṯo nafəqwo Šex Saʕid, u ʕəsyan dak kurmanǧ. Nafəqiwo ʕəsyan. Bəṯər Atatürk dəšiwole, šnəqwole Šex Saʕid w šnəqwole ġalabe ʕamo bi masalayo.
data.translation: Uncle Ishoʕ: Yes, it was. At that time Sheikh Said had just risen up, the revolt of the Kurds. They had risen in revolt. Afterwards Atatürk had crushed it; he had hanged Sheikh Said and he had hanged many people over that affair.

rationale: New Preterit-wa cell for retained round-1 figurative I.3; revolt explicitly introduced.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 1.39/1741)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Afandəm, huwewo laǧan d mdafʕina ʕal u qazayḏan, d misomo Məḏyaḏ walaye. Mdafʕinawo ġalabe. Mdafʕinawo d misomo walaye. W bəṯər d əḏʕina ḥaq diḏan daṣ ṣəroye, d məḏʕinale. D lowe mədone naḥaqqiye aʕlayna, d midəšina qəm di raġlo. Čike məḏʕinawo b ḥaq diḏan. Huwewolan taṯirat, mʕawniwolan. Maʕlum yo, i naqqa d mawḏəʕinawo, l əḏʕiwo d kito ṣəroye b Məḏyaḏ. L əḏʕiwo d kito ṣəroye b Məḏyaḏ, əšmo wayna b Tərkiya.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: Sir, it used to be so that we could defend our district, that Midyat be made a province. We used to advocate a great deal. We advocated that it be made a province. And afterwards, that we know our rights as Christians, that we make them known. That there should be no unjust things against us, that we should not be trampled underfoot. We used to make our rights known a little. We had influence; they would help us. Of course, when we used to inform them, they did not know that there were Christians in Midyat. They did not know that there were Christians in Midyat, that we amounted to something in Turkey.

rationale: New Detransitive Infectum and sense; oppression image with rights context. Negation scope provisional.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 3 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.35/5539)

data.turoyo: Uṯanwo ay yawnoye duʕriwo aʕlayye, dayšiwolan. W dayəma fayšina taḥt i dawse. Haṯe ste m aṯarla aʕlayna ġalabe. At tre mədonani ste m aṯarre aʕlayna.
data.translation: The Greeks would come, turn back against them, and trample us. And we always remain under the trampling. This too has affected us greatly. Both these things have affected us.

rationale: New I.3 Infectum-wa cell: political oppression rather than literal crop treading.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/631)

data.turoyo: B briṯo kula, kiban d əmmina, an niše komidoši. U medano ġalabe aṯrawoṯe komaqbəlile. W mawxa ste layto ʕaǧubo d əmmina: ‘An niše d bayn du ʕamayḏan ste komidoši’.
data.translation: Throughout the world, we can say, women are being trampled on. Many countries accept this matter. And so it is no wonder that we say: “Women among our people are being trampled on too.”

rationale: New I Detransitive Infectum: overt women subject and repeated agentless predication.

summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 4.II/814)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni am mədonani ne, u ʕamayḏan u durošo, yaʕni i iḏaʕṯo ġalabe noquṣṭo yo, xəd kuḏʕina mən šəkəl diše wayna bu aṯro.
data.translation: That is, these are the things: our people, education, that is, knowledge is very deficient; as we know, how we were trampled on in the homeland.

rationale: New I Detransitive Part. Pass. box; diše with past copula.

summary: example for sense 5 in Preterit (Jan 2.5/1511)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Bann 44 (1944) hawino afədyaqno, qoriyo afədyaqno, qoriyo mzawnoyo. Bann 44 hawino afədyaqno w bəṯər mə d dəšlan bann 60 (1960), hawino arxedyaqon, riše da mšamšone w bəṯər b 14 yarḥe hawino qašo.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (Jan 4.I/600)

data.turoyo: Bas ono kḥozeno oluṯo rabṯo d MED TV d mḥaḏər taḥrasyoṯe hawxa, d moyəd mawquf mqabəl daḥ ḥaylanək d kətwayne ḥayle fanatikoye ṭaye mʔaxre, dəšše u ʕamayḏan, d qṭəlle u ʕamayḏan.

summary: New idiom: dəšle/doyəš raġlo b- 'den Fuß über eine Schwelle setzen'

summary: New idiom: dəšle/doyəš ʕal ʕayne d- 'bei jemandem herzlich willkommen sein'

data.headword: dəšle/doyəš ʕal ʕayne d- 'bei jemandem herzlich willkommen sein'
data.turoyo: me tamo larke, ʕal ʕayni w d babi dəšlux

summary: Physical affected targets use ʕal/aʕl- (person, body parts, surface); material/crop patients and raġli also occur without a preposition. b- marks vehicle, foot instrument or location in the threshold expression.
ko-Preterit locates the accident retrospectively; Infectum-wa describes customary animal threshing. These are independent of the semantic subdivision.

Exhortative duš is abundant in PrS, occurs with a female addressee and alternates with plural dušu; JTM has Dəš. This suggests partial lexicalization, without proving invariant agreement in every dialect.

Dušulle at PrS 15/43 and 61/124 is a directed exhortation in a hostile context; a separate lexical attack sense is not demonstrated. Abstract honour and feud uses share the figurative sense, while welcoming on the host's eyes is a fixed formula.
Lookup searches ʕayni, ʕal ʕayn, raġli, doyəš raġ and admawo found no matching dyš idiom record; qbl and ṭyr contain comparable eye-based welcome language.
The pressure construction differs from disregard/oppression: ʕal marks the person moved to act and d introduces the requested action. Human agents and circumstances alternate.

Temporal entry has b-marked age or calendar year; suffixes -li/-lan in age formulae require checking against ordinary l-agent inflection. The source does not decide an impersonal analysis, so the gloss leaves person coding open.

I Detransitive Infectum midoš and Part. Pass. diše suppress the external agent and foreground oppressed people/women. Negation at 1741 is supplied by discourse scope, not a separate negative morpheme on midəšina.
Round-1 active senses 2 and 3 and its ko-Preterit/Infinitiv boxes are retained. No active senses are renumbered; new ones start at 4.
Confirm whether duš is invariant with female addressees (PrS 34/67, 60/75, 76/10, 79/11), and whether Dusu at PrS 84/5 represents spelling or pronunciation.
Is duš + raġlo b- productive, or specifically a conventional set-foot construction? Only the threshold expression is directly evidenced here.
Check reference systems: near-identical existing prs 101/1 versus supplied PrS 37/88, and existing prs 50/4 versus PrS 20/10. No citation replacement is justified from these inputs alone.

PrS 43/9 embeds a verse-10 clause without its German translation; PrS 43/11 does not translate Duš. Neither is quoted as an added example. Some supplied verses end in an unclosed quotation; cuts preserve their source wording.
Confirm ordinary l-agent versus experiencer interpretation of dəšwoli/dəšwolan in age formulae and the exact age boundary at 1073.
At 1741 does preceding d lowe scope over d midəšina? At 631 confirm komidoši as the I Detransitive rather than a separate borrowed verb.
At Jan 4.I/543 does dəšše ʕal ak kewe mean discuss the pains, or undergo/dwell on them? No discussion sense is published from this line.
Does political crushing in dəšiwole (1341) require a conventional active subsense beyond round-1 I.3? It is retained as a participant extension here.
Material processing by literal treading: cement compaction, animal threshing, grape pressing. The direct object and purposeful result do not on their own establish separate technical meanings.
Grape processing supports the literal material-treading extension already recorded in round 1.
Jan supports round-1 figurative trampling with rights, peoples and suppression of revolt. Political reference does not automatically create an additional sense.
